Article 25

(1) The community can actively participate in providing protection for women and children.

(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. conducting prevention and reporting cases of violence against women and children that occur in their residential environment; b. providing emergency assistance if there is violence against women and children;
c. initiating the establishment of women and children protection institutions at the regional, sub-district, village and sub-district levels;
d. participating in the protection of women and children through existing service institutions; and/or
e. assisting in the repatriation, social rehabilitation, and social reintegration process.

Article 5

(1) Prevention of violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a is implemented through:

a. planning and implementation of policies, programs, and activities; b. provision of education; and
c. enhancement of community participation.
(2) Prevention of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regional Government in an integrated and continuous manner based on the Regional Long-Term Development Plan and Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
(3) Planning and implementation of policies, programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a namely:
a. integrating women and children protection issues into the policies, programs and activities of Regional Apparatus; and
b. making women and children protection issues one of the regional development priorities.
(4) Provision of education as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b namely: a. providing information, guidance and/or counseling; b. providing accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement and social services;
c. creating a friendly and safe work environment atmosphere for women; and
d. developing and providing an easily accessible information system; (5) Enhancement of Community participation through involvement of parties as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, namely:
a. building and increasing community participation and awareness regarding prevention and protection of women and children; b. making regional regulations and encouraging Village Governments to make Village Regulations related to the protection of women and children; and
c. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, private sector/business world, universities, mass media, and non-governmental organizations as well as community institutions that work and care for women and children.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Bulukumba Regency.
2. Government is the body or organization that exercises the governmental power of a state. The Government has the duty to administer governmental affairs, from the central, provincial, regency, municipal, sub-district, urban village, to village levels.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is the organization/institution within the regional government that is responsible to the Regent in the administration of government consisting of the regional secretariat, regional agencies and regional technical institutions, sub-districts, villages and civil service police units according to regional needs.
5. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that has the principal duties and functions in carrying out Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Bulukumba Regency.
6. Village Government is the administration of governmental affairs and the interests of the local community within the governmental system of the unitary state of the Republic of Indonesia.
7. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the annual financial plan of the regional government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives, and established by Regional Regulation.
8. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter referred to as APBDes, is the annual financial plan of the village government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Village Head and the Village Representative Body established through Village Regulation.
9. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
10. Administration of Women and Child Protection is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort conducted by the Central Government, Regional Government, Village Government, and community to fulfill the rights of women and children as citizens within the scope of this Regional Regulation.
11. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Women and Child Protection is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
13. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
16. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, and deprivation of liberty arbitrarily whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
17. Victim is a person who experiences physical suffering, women and children who experience violence and/or mental threats and or economic loss caused by an act of violence.
18. Victim of Violence is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering caused by an act of violent crime.
19. Violence Prevention is any action or effort taken to eliminate various factors that cause acts of violence against women and children.
20. Community is an individual Indonesian citizen, community group, and/or civil society organization.
21. Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA, is an operational technical implementation unit within the work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an integrated service provider for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems.
22. Child-Friendly Regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
23. Assistance for Victims of Violence is an effort or process to assist victims of violence in accessing their rights to handling, protection, and recovery.
24. Rapid Response Team, hereinafter abbreviated as TRC, is a team formed by the agency responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection whose duty is to assist UPT PPA in conducting outreach and/or assistance to expedite the process of handling cases of violence against women and children.
25. Task Force for Women and Child Protection is a coordinative institution formed by the Bulukumba Regency Government that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Bulukumba Regency.
26. Vulnerable Groups are any person or group of people who have the right to receive special treatment and protection relating to their specificity. Vulnerable Groups as referred to in this regulation consist of women and children in conflict with the law, persons with disabilities, Indonesian migrant workers, the elderly and/or the indigenous people of ammatoa Kajang.

Letter a

What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect for and protection of the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status. This means that women and children have the same right to live without violence and treatment that degrades human dignity.

Letter b

What is meant by the principle of justice and gender equality is this principle emphasizes the need to address gender inequality which is often the root cause of acts of violence against women and children. Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.

Letter c

What is meant by the principle of protection is proactive and preventive protection against acts of violence. This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims and potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.

What is meant by the principle of the best interests of women and children is this principle focuses on the best interests and rights of women and children as the top priority. Protection actions and policies must always prioritize their welfare and interests, including listening to their views and aspirations in the decision-making process.

Letter e

What is meant by the principle of non-discrimination is this principle affirms that protection must be carried out without discrimination based on gender, age, ethnic background, religion, or social status. Every individual has the same right to be protected from acts of violence, without exception

Letter f

What is meant by the principle of special treatment for vulnerable groups is treatment toward a group of people who experience vulnerability or physical and non-physical limitations such as women, children, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, the elderly, minority groups, people with mental disorders and the poor.

NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 17

(1) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 16, the Regent establishes programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the form of a regional action plan as a basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing the protection of women and children.

(2) The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.

CHAPTER III

SCOPE

Article 7

(1) Victim assistance as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2) letter f includes all integrated efforts to restore and strengthen the victim's condition.

(2) Victim assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by UPT PPA.

(3) Victim assistance is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 19

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector as referred to in Article 15 letter c are carried out in the form of private sector participation. (2) The role of the private sector as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. providing protection for women and children through corporate social and environmental responsibility programs;

b. providing support to the government, community institutions, civil society organizations and the community in the context of the protection of women and children; and

c. actively participating in business organizations that have a commitment to the protection of women and children.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

11. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Women and Child Protection is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
13. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

16. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, and deprivation of liberty arbitrarily whether occurring in the private or public sphere.

22. 9. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.

11. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Women and Child Protection is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
13. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect for and protection of the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status. CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 25

(1) The community can actively participate in providing protection for women and children.

(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. conducting prevention and reporting cases of violence against women and children that occur in their residential environment; b. providing emergency assistance if there is violence against women and children;
c. initiating the establishment of women and children protection institutions at the regional, sub-district, village and sub-district levels;
d. participating in the protection of women and children through existing service institutions; and/or
e. assisting in the repatriation, social rehabilitation, and social reintegration process.

d. providing character education and instilling moral values in Children

Article 17

(1) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 16, the Regent establishes programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the form of a regional action plan as a basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing the protection of women and children.

(2) The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector as referred to in Article 15 letter c are carried out in the form of private sector participation. c. actively participating in business organizations that have a commitment to the protection of women and children.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

22. COOPERATION

Article 25

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect for and protection of the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status. This means that women and children have the same right to live without violence and treatment that degrades human dignity.

Letter b

What is meant by the principle of justice and gender equality is this principle emphasizes the need to address gender inequality which is often the root cause of acts of violence against women and children. Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.

Letter c

What is meant by the principle of protection is proactive and preventive protection against acts of violence. This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims and potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.

Letter d

What is meant by the principle of the best interests of women and children is this principle focuses on the best interests and rights of women and children as the top priority. Protection actions and policies must always prioritize their welfare and interests, including listening to their views and aspirations in the decision-making process.

Letter e

What is meant by the principle of non-discrimination is this principle affirms that protection must be carried out without discrimination based on gender, age, ethnic background, religion, or social status. CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

4. Regional Apparatus is the organization/institution within the regional government that is responsible to the Regent in the administration of government consisting of the regional secretariat, regional agencies and regional technical institutions, sub-districts, villages and civil service police units according to regional needs.

13. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
16. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, and deprivation of liberty arbitrarily whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
17. Victim is a person who experiences physical suffering, women and children who experience violence and/or mental threats and or economic loss caused by an act of violence.
18. Victim of Violence is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering caused by an act of violent crime.
19. Violence Prevention is any action or effort taken to eliminate various factors that cause acts of violence against women and children.
20. Community is an individual Indonesian citizen, community group, and/or civil society organization.
21. Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA, is an operational technical implementation unit within the work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an integrated service provider for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems.
22. c. initiating the establishment of women and children protection institutions at the regional, sub-district, village and sub-district levels;
d. participating in the protection of women and children through existing service institutions; and/or
e. assisting in the repatriation, social rehabilitation, and social reintegration process.

Article 2

Letter a

Letter b

What is meant by the principle of justice and gender equality is this principle emphasizes the need to address gender inequality which is often the root cause of acts of violence against women and children. Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.

Letter c

What is meant by the principle of protection is proactive and preventive protection against acts of violence. This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims and potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.

Letter d

What is meant by the principle of the best interests of women and children is this principle focuses on the best interests and rights of women and children as the top priority. Letter e

What is meant by the principle of non-discrimination is this principle affirms that protection must be carried out without discrimination based on gender, age, ethnic background, religion, or social status. What is meant by the principle of special treatment for vulnerable groups is treatment toward a group of people who experience vulnerability or physical and non-physical limitations such as women, children, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, the elderly, minority groups, people with mental disorders and the poor.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

Article 17

Article 19

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector as referred to in Article 15 letter c are carried out in the form of private sector participation. (2) The role of the private sector as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. providing protection for women and children through corporate social and environmental responsibility programs;

b. providing support to the government, community institutions, civil society organizations and the community in the context of the protection of women and children; and

c. actively participating in business organizations that have a commitment to the protection of women and children.

4. 17. Victim is a person who experiences physical suffering, women and children who experience violence and/or mental threats and or economic loss caused by an act of violence.

Article 25

(1) The community can actively participate in providing protection for women and children.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect for and protection of the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status. Letter e

Letter f

What is meant by the principle of special treatment for vulnerable groups is treatment toward a group of people who experience vulnerability or physical and non-physical limitations such as women, children, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, the elderly, minority groups, people with mental disorders and the poor.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

(1) The community can actively participate in providing protection for women and children.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

NUMBER 3 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 26

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
c. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

This means that women and children have the same right to live without violence and treatment that degrades human dignity.

Letter b

What is meant by the principle of justice and gender equality is this principle emphasizes the need to address gender inequality which is often the root cause of acts of violence against women and children. Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.

What is meant by the principle of protection is proactive and preventive protection against acts of violence. This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims and potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.

Article 25

(1) The community can actively participate in providing protection for women and children.

(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. conducting prevention and reporting cases of violence against women and children that occur in their residential environment; b. providing emergency assistance if there is violence against women and children;
c. initiating the establishment of women and children protection institutions at the regional, sub-district, village and sub-district levels;
d. participating in the protection of women and children through existing service institutions; and/or
e. assisting in the repatriation, social rehabilitation, and social reintegration process.

Article 5

(1) Prevention of violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a is implemented through:

a. planning and implementation of policies, programs, and activities; b. provision of education; and
c. enhancement of community participation.
(2) Prevention of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regional Government in an integrated and continuous manner based on the Regional Long-Term Development Plan and Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
(3) Planning and implementation of policies, programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a namely:
a. integrating women and children protection issues into the policies, programs and activities of Regional Apparatus; and
b. making women and children protection issues one of the regional development priorities.
(4) Provision of education as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b namely: a. providing information, guidance and/or counseling; b. providing accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement and social services;
c. creating a friendly and safe work environment atmosphere for women; and
d. developing and providing an easily accessible information system; (5) Enhancement of Community participation through involvement of parties as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, namely:
a. building and increasing community participation and awareness regarding prevention and protection of women and children; b. making regional regulations and encouraging Village Governments to make Village Regulations related to the protection of women and children; and
c. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, private sector/business world, universities, mass media, and non-governmental organizations as well as community institutions that work and care for women and children.

Article 7

(1) Victim assistance as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2) letter f includes all integrated efforts to restore and strengthen the victim's condition.

(2) Victim assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by UPT PPA.

(3) Victim assistance is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 17

(1) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 16, the Regent establishes programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the form of a regional action plan as a basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing the protection of women and children.

(2) The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.

SCOPE

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Bulukumba Regency.
2. Government is the body or organization that exercises the governmental power of a state. The Government has the duty to administer governmental affairs, from the central, provincial, regency, municipal, sub-district, urban village, to village levels.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is the organization/institution within the regional government that is responsible to the Regent in the administration of government consisting of the regional secretariat, regional agencies and regional technical institutions, sub-districts, villages and civil service police units according to regional needs.
5. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that has the principal duties and functions in carrying out Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Bulukumba Regency.
6. Village Government is the administration of governmental affairs and the interests of the local community within the governmental system of the unitary state of the Republic of Indonesia.
7. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the annual financial plan of the regional government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives, and established by Regional Regulation.
8. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter referred to as APBDes, is the annual financial plan of the village government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Village Head and the Village Representative Body established through Village Regulation.
9. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
10. Administration of Women and Child Protection is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort conducted by the Central Government, Regional Government, Village Government, and community to fulfill the rights of women and children as citizens within the scope of this Regional Regulation.
11. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Women and Child Protection is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
13. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
16. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, and deprivation of liberty arbitrarily whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
17. Victim is a person who experiences physical suffering, women and children who experience violence and/or mental threats and or economic loss caused by an act of violence.
18. Victim of Violence is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering caused by an act of violent crime.
19. Violence Prevention is any action or effort taken to eliminate various factors that cause acts of violence against women and children.
20. Community is an individual Indonesian citizen, community group, and/or civil society organization.
21. Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA, is an operational technical implementation unit within the work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an integrated service provider for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems.
22. Child-Friendly Regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
23. Assistance for Victims of Violence is an effort or process to assist victims of violence in accessing their rights to handling, protection, and recovery.
24. Rapid Response Team, hereinafter abbreviated as TRC, is a team formed by the agency responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection whose duty is to assist UPT PPA in conducting outreach and/or assistance to expedite the process of handling cases of violence against women and children.
25. Task Force for Women and Child Protection is a coordinative institution formed by the Bulukumba Regency Government that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Bulukumba Regency.
26. Vulnerable Groups are any person or group of people who have the right to receive special treatment and protection relating to their specificity. Vulnerable Groups as referred to in this regulation consist of women and children in conflict with the law, persons with disabilities, Indonesian migrant workers, the elderly and/or the indigenous people of ammatoa Kajang.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect for and protection of the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status. This means that women and children have the same right to live without violence and treatment that degrades human dignity.

Letter b

What is meant by the principle of justice and gender equality is this principle emphasizes the need to address gender inequality which is often the root cause of acts of violence against women and children. Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.

Letter c

What is meant by the principle of protection is proactive and preventive protection against acts of violence. This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims and potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.

Letter d

What is meant by the principle of the best interests of women and children is this principle focuses on the best interests and rights of women and children as the top priority. Protection actions and policies must always prioritize their welfare and interests, including listening to their views and aspirations in the decision-making process.

Letter e

What is meant by the principle of non-discrimination is this principle affirms that protection must be carried out without discrimination based on gender, age, ethnic background, religion, or social status. Every individual has the same right to be protected from acts of violence, without exception

What is meant by the principle of special treatment for vulnerable groups is treatment toward a group of people who experience vulnerability or physical and non-physical limitations such as women, children, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, the elderly, minority groups, people with mental disorders and the poor.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect for and protection of the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status. This means that women and children have the same right to live without violence and treatment that degrades human dignity.

Letter b

What is meant by the principle of justice and gender equality is this principle emphasizes the need to address gender inequality which is often the root cause of acts of violence against women and children. Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.

Letter c

What is meant by the principle of protection is proactive and preventive protection against acts of violence. This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims and potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.

Letter d

What is meant by the principle of the best interests of women and children is this principle focuses on the best interests and rights of women and children as the top priority. Protection actions and policies must always prioritize their welfare and interests, including listening to their views and aspirations in the decision-making process.

Letter e

What is meant by the principle of non-discrimination is this principle affirms that protection must be carried out without discrimination based on gender, age, ethnic background, religion, or social status. Every individual has the same right to be protected from acts of violence, without exception

Letter f

What is meant by the principle of special treatment for vulnerable groups is treatment toward a group of people who experience vulnerability or physical and non-physical limitations such as women, children, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, the elderly, minority groups, people with mental disorders and the poor.

Article 25

(1) The community can actively participate in providing protection for women and children.

(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. conducting prevention and reporting cases of violence against women and children that occur in their residential environment; b. providing emergency assistance if there is violence against women and children;
c. initiating the establishment of women and children protection institutions at the regional, sub-district, village and sub-district levels;
d. participating in the protection of women and children through existing service institutions; and/or
e. assisting in the repatriation, social rehabilitation, and social reintegration process.

7. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the annual financial plan of the regional government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives, and established by Regional Regulation.
8. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter referred to as APBDes, is the annual financial plan of the village government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Village Head and the Village Representative Body established through Village Regulation.
9. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
10. Administration of Women and Child Protection is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort conducted by the Central Government, Regional Government, Village Government, and community to fulfill the rights of women and children as citizens within the scope of this Regional Regulation.
11. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Women and Child Protection is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
13. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
16. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, and deprivation of liberty arbitrarily whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
17. Victim is a person who experiences physical suffering, women and children who experience violence and/or mental threats and or economic loss caused by an act of violence.
18. Victim of Violence is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering caused by an act of violent crime.
19. Violence Prevention is any action or effort taken to eliminate various factors that cause acts of violence against women and children.
20. Community is an individual Indonesian citizen, community group, and/or civil society organization.
21. Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA, is an operational technical implementation unit within the work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an integrated service provider for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems.
22. Child-Friendly Regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
23. Assistance for Victims of Violence is an effort or process to assist victims of violence in accessing their rights to handling, protection, and recovery.
24. Rapid Response Team, hereinafter abbreviated as TRC, is a team formed by the agency responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection whose duty is to assist UPT PPA in conducting outreach and/or assistance to expedite the process of handling cases of violence against women and children.
25. Task Force for Women and Child Protection is a coordinative institution formed by the Bulukumba Regency Government that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Bulukumba Regency.
26. Vulnerable Groups are any person or group of people who have the right to receive special treatment and protection relating to their specificity. Vulnerable Groups as referred to in this regulation consist of women and children in conflict with the law, persons with disabilities, Indonesian migrant workers, the elderly and/or the indigenous people of ammatoa Kajang.

Article 5

(1) Prevention of violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a is implemented through:

a. planning and implementation of policies, programs, and activities; b. provision of education; and
c. enhancement of community participation.
(2) Prevention of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regional Government in an integrated and continuous manner based on the Regional Long-Term Development Plan and Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
(3) Planning and implementation of policies, programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a namely:
a. integrating women and children protection issues into the policies, programs and activities of Regional Apparatus; and
b. making women and children protection issues one of the regional development priorities.
(4) Provision of education as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b namely: a. providing information, guidance and/or counseling; b. providing accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement and social services;
c. creating a friendly and safe work environment atmosphere for women; and
d. developing and providing an easily accessible information system; (5) Enhancement of Community participation through involvement of parties as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, namely:
a. building and increasing community participation and awareness regarding prevention and protection of women and children; b. making regional regulations and encouraging Village Governments to make Village Regulations related to the protection of women and children; and
c. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, private sector/business world, universities, mass media, and non-governmental organizations as well as community institutions that work and care for women and children.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.
